These racks feature 102.4 terabits per second switch blades using 128 ports of 800G connections, powered by Broadcom Tomahawk 6C and NVIDIA Spectrum-6 variants. The innovation directly supports Meta's latest AI models—Muse Wonder and Muse Spark—and their Prometheus cluster, which operates at gigawatt scale. The liquid-cooling approach represents a major shift from traditional air-cooled networking infrastructure, enabling higher density deployments and more efficient power consumption. By open-sourcing these designs through OCP, Meta is essentially giving the entire AI industry a blueprint for scaling compute clusters without hitting thermal or power delivery walls. This matters because as AI models get larger and require more interconnected GPUs and TPUs, the networking layer becomes a critical bottleneck—data moving between processors generates massive heat, and traditional air cooling can't keep up. IcePack and IceCube solve this by circulating coolant directly through the network hardware, allowing for tighter packaging and higher performance per unit of space and power.

articles.hook: Open ASR just got way more diverse with African English.
articles.headline: Egyptian and Nigerian English now on Open ASR Leaderboard
articles.body: HuggingFace's Open ASR Leaderboard has expanded to include automatic speech recognition (ASR) models trained on Egyptian Arabic English and Nigerian English, marking a significant step toward more inclusive AI language coverage. The leaderboard, which benchmarks open-source speech recognition systems across multiple languages and dialects, previously had limited representation from African English variants despite the hundreds of millions of speakers across the continent. This addition allows developers and researchers to evaluate how well ASR systems perform on these underrepresented dialects, exposing gaps where commercial models often fail. Egyptian English and Nigerian English have distinct phonetic, prosodic, and linguistic characteristics shaped by substrate influences from Arabic and local Nigerian languages respectively, making them challenging for models trained primarily on Western English data. By including these variants on a public leaderboard, HuggingFace is incentivizing the AI community to build better models for African speakers, directly addressing the accessibility gap that has excluded these populations from voice AI tools. The move reflects growing momentum in making AI infrastructure more representative and is crucial for entrepreneurs building voice applications across Africa who need reliable benchmarks to test their systems.

articles.headline: NVIDIA Cosmos 3: Open Models for Building Interactive Virtual Worlds
articles.body: NVIDIA has released Cosmos 3, a new family of open-source foundation models designed for interactive world simulation. These models can generate and understand dynamic 3D environments that respond to user input in real-time, moving beyond static video generation into fully interactive virtual spaces. Cosmos 3 represents a significant step forward in generative AI by enabling developers to create simulations that don't just play out predetermined sequences but instead adapt and evolve based on actions taken within them. The models are being released openly on HuggingFace, allowing entrepreneurs and researchers to build applications without licensing restrictions. Key capabilities include the ability to simulate physics interactions, generate coherent long-form sequences, and maintain consistency across complex scenes. Compared to previous world models that produced short, often incoherent clips, Cosmos 3 demonstrates improved temporal stability and spatial reasoning. This opens immediate applications in robotics training, game development, autonomous vehicle simulation, and digital twin creation—all areas where previously companies had to build custom simulators from scratch. The open-source release means developers can fine-tune and customize these models for specific use cases rather than waiting for proprietary APIs.
